signals.summary: A cluster of fresh coverage on Europe's overnight and scenic rail: new cross-border connections, record-long routes, and luxury upgrades are pushing rail journeys as the headline way to see the continent this summer.
signals.why_now: 5+ independent recent items: The Australian 'The world's most legendary train just got an Amalfi upgrade' (9h), Time Out 'Has this new train connection created Europe's longest rail journey?' (40h), The Independent 'Two European countries connected by train for first time in decades - with tickets from £4.60' (62h) and 'The best affordable sleeper train journeys to take in 2026' (93h), Business Insider sleeper-cabin diary (37h). Corroborated by stale evergreens (Forbes 'Overnight Trains Are Booming', Condé Nast, T+L). Reddit was unavailable, so this rests on news/RSS alone.

signals.summary: Slow travel remains a broad, steadily-fed wave: readers are being pushed toward longer stays in one place, nature detoxes, and unhurried regional trips rather than checklist itineraries.
signals.why_now: 9+ independent items, many fresh: Everyday Tourist 'The Detour Is The Destination: A Slow-Travel Guide To Small Prairie Cities' (14h), Times of India family who 'sold our house' for a European country (21h), EIN 'Rise of Slow Travel: Dark Sky Lofts in Sedona' (34h), Mshale Curacao 6-months (46h), Nine.com.au Forster 'slow travel detox' (50h), Guardian 'A slow, boozy bus tour of Hungary's secret vineyards' (66h), Soul of Hospitality Tree of Life Himalaya (69h), TheGATE Victoria Australia nature escapes (74h), Colorado Parent (155h). Evergreen theme, so older ranking pieces (T+L Japan, AFAR) are supporting not load-bearing.

signals.summary: Fresh interest in night-sky destinations and unplugged, dark-sky stays lands right on the late-summer meteor-shower window, framing starry landscapes as the escape of the moment.
signals.why_now: Two fresh independent anchors plus a supporting evergreen: Euronews 'Ranked: The world's best stargazing destinations - and the No.1 is in France' (23h) and EIN 'The Rise of Slow Travel: Why Dark Sky Lofts in Sedona Is a Destination for Restoration' (34h), reinforced by T+L 'These European Destinations Are the Top Spots for a Screen-free Getaway' (stale). Timely against the mid-August Perseid peak. Small pool and Reddit was down, so treated as a modest-velocity but highly-producible seasonal wave.

signals.summary: A recurring pull toward uncrowded 'secret' beaches, lakes and off-list regional destinations - the quieter alternative to overtouristed hotspots.
signals.why_now: Several independent items, two recent: Storyboard18 'ixigo taps rap to urge Gen Z to explore India's hidden travel destinations' (21h) and New Jersey Monthly '7 of Our Favorite Hidden Beaches in New Jersey' (58h), plus National Geographic 'Europe's secret lakes - 6 destinations without the crowds' and T+L scenic-island boating study (both older but on-theme). A diffuse but persistent late-summer crowd-avoidance wave; Reddit unavailable so leaning on news only.

signals.summary: Wellness travel keeps surfacing as a positioning play - hotel wellness collaborations and 24-hour bathhouse culture selling serene spa interiors and thermal soaks as the destination itself.
signals.why_now: Modest but distinct pool: TravelPulse 'Marriott Embraces Wellness Travel Trend With New Collaboration' (14h) and National Geographic 'Why China's 24-Hour Spas are the Hottest New Travel Trend' (112h), plus the Sedona 'restoration' framing (34h). Skews trade-press, so scored cautiously on velocity; the imagery (steam rooms, thermal pools, calm interiors) is what carries it.

signals.summary: Economic pressure is shifting travelers toward shorter, cheaper, nearer trips and 'urban basecamp' stays in midsize cities rather than long-haul flagship destinations.
signals.why_now: Fresh Skift anchor 'Travel Creators Follow the Money to Shorter Trips' (14h) alongside Skift's overseas-arrivals-to-US decline (11h), reinforced by the (older) 'urban basecamp' pieces from ktvu and ABC30 and Axios 'closer, cheaper trips'. A genuine macro theme but mostly a behavioral/economic story and image-abstract, so scored lower on fit and producibility. Reddit outage weakens corroboration.
